0.10.0 is a score release. rust-doctor scanned its own repository, and each place where the score, the report or a detector claimed more than the code held was fixed. The score moves to model core-v6 and the JSON report to schema 24, two noisy Clippy rules become opt-in, a manifest `[lints]` allow is now honored, and the duplicate, size and allow detectors only report what holds. On the 18 pinned corpus projects no score moves more than 5 points. A scan also survives input that used to crash it, a CRLF checkout parses as rustc reads it, and `cargo binstall rust-doctor` now installs a prebuilt binary. Scores are not comparable with 0.9.0: read [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes) before you compare them or parse the report.

## Breaking changes

### Scores move to model core-v6, and the JSON report to schema 24

**Before.** Model `core-v5`, schema 23. A withheld rule (one the corpus found wrong on most of the sites it reviewed) still capped its dimension. The score counted the lines of inline `#[cfg(test)]` items as production code. A duplicate crate version pulled in only by a dependency weighed like one you require directly.

**After.** `audit.score.model` is `core-v6` and `schema_version` is `24` ([8774eb6](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8774eb6), [5cd4592](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/5cd4592)):

- A withheld rule caps no dimension. The score still charges its sites, with its discount.
- The ranking of what to fix first applies a measured rule's discount once, not twice.
- Outermost inline items carrying `#[cfg(test)]`, and `#[test]` functions, leave `audit.production_lines`. A crate with inline test modules has fewer production lines, so its densities rise.
- `rust_doctor::cargo::duplicate_major_versions` publishes a duplicate that no member requires directly at `info`, with its `base_severity` kept. It no longer weighs on the score, fails a `--blocking warning` gate or blocks the agent hook. Versions now compare by Cargo compatibility class (`M`, `0.m`, `0.0.p`), so `0.59.0` beside `0.61.2` is now reported and `1.4.0` beside `1.9.2` still is not. The message reads "incompatible versions" instead of "incompatible major versions", which changes every id of that rule. The rule has no corpus rate under core-v6, so a lone direct duplicate scores 72 on dependencies instead of 75.
- Schema 24 adds two fields:
  - `audit.score.ceilings`: one entry per capped dimension, then `overall` last. For example `{"dimension": "security", "tier": "P1", "ceiling": 50, "rule_ids": ["clippy::permissions_set_readonly_false"]}`. The list is empty when no tier caps.
  - `audit.categories[].production`: the `errors`, `warnings`, `info`, `unknown` and `total` that weigh on the score, beside `occurrences`, which still counts everything.
- `worst_tier` is now the worst tier that caps, so a withheld or uncatalogued rule no longer sets it.
- The share link's `e`, `w` and `i` count production findings only. On this repository's self-scan, 140 of 192 warnings weighed nothing.

| Value | 0.9.0 | 0.10.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `SCORE_MODEL` | `core-v5` | `core-v6` |
| `SCHEMA_VERSION` | 23 | 24 |
| `duplicate_function_body` corpus noise | 4091 bp (8 of 20) | 3500 bp (6 of 18) |
| `near_duplicate_function_body` corpus noise | 6250 bp (19 of 30) | 6129 bp (18 of 29), still withheld |
| `duplicate_major_versions` corpus noise | 3333 bp (0 of 1) | unmeasured, 5000 bp |
| Lone direct major-version duplicate, dependencies | 75 | 72 |

The tier ceilings, the density constants and the category mappings do not change.

| Population | Project | 0.9.0 | 0.10.0 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| healthy | anyhow | 73 | 73 |
| healthy | async-channel | 97 | 97 |
| healthy | bytes | 82 | 82 |
| healthy | fd | 87 | 86 |
| healthy | hexyl | 93 | 93 |
| healthy | log | 90 | 90 |
| healthy | ripgrep | 90 | 91 |
| healthy | serde_json | 88 | 88 |
| healthy | smol | 100 | 100 |
| healthy | thiserror | 85 | 88 |
| agent-written | claudes-c-compiler | 82 | 82 |
| agent-written | ostendo | 79 | 80 |
| agent-written | artifexprocal | 90 | 89 |
| agent-written | mdr | 65 | 65 |
| agent-written | ralph-os | 89 | 89 |
| agent-written | vibesql | 58 | 58 |
| agent-written | syncvibe | 80 | 80 |
| agent-written | coda | 88 | 83 |

The healthy median stays 89 and the agent-written median 81, so the two populations stay 8 points apart.

**Who is affected.** Anyone who compares a 0.10.0 score with a 0.9.0 one, checks `schema_version == 23`, filters `duplicate_major_versions` findings by id, or reads the share link's counts.

**Upgrade path.** Rescan with 0.10.0 before you compare. A `--scope baseline` run is unaffected: it scans both sides with the same binary, and its base-side cache is keyed on the crate version and the schema. `rust-doctor report` and `why --report` still read saved reports from schema 20 to 24. A JSON consumer accepts `24` and may read the two new fields:

```bash
rust-doctor inspect --json . --yes | jq '.schema_version, .audit.score.model, .audit.score.ceilings'
```

### `clippy::indexing_slicing` and `clippy::string_slice` are off by default

**Before.** Both ran at `warn`. **After.** Both ship at `default_level: off`. They stay catalogued as reliability P3 rules, and the catalog still holds 142 rules, but a default scan runs 102 of the 104 Clippy rules and no longer passes `-W` for these two. The pinned corpus found each one wrong on all 40 of its reviewed sites, with no true positive ([8ed9985](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8ed9985)).

**Who is affected.** Anyone who relied on either rule. Their sites no longer appear and no longer weigh, so a score can rise.

**Upgrade path.** Switch them back on for one run, or for the workspace in `rust-doctor.toml`. A `warn` in a manifest's `[lints]` table is not enough, since the scan drops a catalogued rule its policy leaves off.

```bash
rust-doctor . --rule clippy::indexing_slicing=warn --rule clippy::string_slice=warn
```

```toml
[rules]
"clippy::indexing_slicing" = "warn"
"clippy::string_slice" = "warn"
```

### A manifest `[lints]` allow now hides the sites it allows

**Before.** The scan passed every catalogued lint as `-W`, which overrode an `allow` in a manifest's `[lints.clippy]` table, so the site was reported and `rust_doctor::cargo::permissive_lint_table` charged the allow as well. **After.** The scan drops, package by package, the Clippy findings that package's `[lints]` allows, entries inherited through `[lints] workspace = true` included. A member's allow hides only that member's sites. `permissive_lint_table` moves from P2 to P3, so the allow is reported once and caps no dimension ([2013077](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/2013077)).

| Tier | 0.9.0 | 0.10.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| P2 | 25 | 24 |
| P3 | 33 | 34 |

`rust-doctor why PATH:LINE` now explains an empty site: "Nothing is reported at {path}:{line}: a [lints] table allows {rules}, so the scan hides those sites there." Its JSON adds the reason `allowed-by-lints` and an `allowed_by_lints` list.

**Who is affected.** Workspaces with `allow` entries in `[lints]`. Their scores can rise, since the allowed sites leave the report.

**Upgrade path.** To see an allowed rule's sites again, set its level explicitly. A level from `--rule`, `rust-doctor.toml` or a category override wins over the manifest:

```bash
rust-doctor . --rule clippy::unwrap_used=warn
```

To clear the `permissive_lint_table` finding itself, its help names three ways: remove the entry and fix what it silences, switch the rule off in `rust-doctor.toml`, or write `# rust-doctor: allow(rust_doctor::cargo::permissive_lint_table) -- reason` above the key.

### The terminal and Markdown reports are worded differently

**Before.** `Scanned N files in X.Xs`, and category tallies equal to the JSON's `occurrences`. **After** ([b24e4b2](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/b24e4b2)):

- The scope line reads `Scored N production files (L lines) in X.Xs; Clippy linted library and binary targets, native rules also read tests`. When `--package` narrows the scan, it names the members, for example `of member a`. When Clippy is off, it says `Clippy did not run`.
- Category tallies and `--verbose` group headings count only what weighs, and put the rest apart, for example `(+3 outside production code, +1 not scored)`. A single site now reads `(1 occurrence)`.

**Who is affected.** Scripts that parse the text output.

**Upgrade path.** Parse `--json`, whose counts are `audit.categories[].occurrences` and, new in schema 24, `audit.categories[].production`.

### A crashing pass reports `pass-panicked`, and the binary no longer exits 101

**Before.** A panic in the Clippy thread published `clippy-thread-failed` on a failed report that dropped the native findings, and a panic in the structure or manifest pass aborted the process with exit 101. **After.** Every pass runs contained. A pass that panics publishes one error, code `pass-panicked`, at its own stage, for example "The structure pass failed; the score is not authoritative." The report is `incomplete` with exit 1 and keeps every other pass's findings. A panic outside any pass prints `rust-doctor: internal error, please report it` on stderr and exits 2 ([d6060ed](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/d6060ed)).

**Who is affected.** Tools that match `clippy-thread-failed` or exit 101.

**Upgrade path.** Match `pass-panicked` in `errors[].code`, and treat exit 2 as a failed run.

## Detectors that only report what holds

- **Duplicate bodies.** `duplicate_function_body` and `near_duplicate_function_body` claim a family only when every pair holds ([1b7c220](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/1b7c220)):
  - A family made only of test cases (`#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]`, `#[rstest]`) is not reported.
  - An item nested in a function body counts as one opaque node, so a helper both copies hold is not reported again as its own family.
  - Macro arguments now enter the fingerprint as tokens, so `assert!(a == b)` and `assert!(a != b)` no longer match.
  - A near-duplicate group is refined so every pair passes the 80 percent threshold, and the published `similarity` is the lowest pair.
  - The fingerprint domain moves to `rust-doctor-structure-normalized-v2`, which changes every family id.
- **`oversized_unit`** counts a function, `impl` or module from its keyword, so its doc comment and attributes no longer push it over the bound. The bounds (1000 lines per file, 500 per module or `impl`, 150 per function) and the published span do not change ([f8a0ab3](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/f8a0ab3)).
- **`crate_level_allow`** fires only on an inner allow that hides something: a Clippy rule the scan runs, `warnings` or a Clippy group while any Clippy rule runs, `dead_code`, `unused` or an `unused_*` lint. A pair naming `unknown_lints`, the toolchain-compatibility shape, stays quiet, and so does test code such as a shared `tests/support/mod.rs` ([e1b0cfe](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/e1b0cfe)).

## The report says what it measured

The terminal, Markdown and interactive reports now say what the score was computed over and what holds it down. None of this changes the score or the JSON ([b24e4b2](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/b24e4b2), [8774eb6](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8774eb6)).

- The five dimension scores follow an authoritative score: `Security 100 · Reliability 75 · Maintainability 100 · Performance 100 · Dependencies 100`. The interactive report shortens them to `Sec · Rel · Maint · Perf · Deps` on a terminal too narrow for the full names.
- Each capped dimension names its ceiling, for example `Reliability 75 (P2 ceiling: clippy::todo)`. The overall cap sentence names only the rules that hold it, and after three it adds `N more`.
- Rules a crate version left unevaluated are listed: `Not evaluated, the crate version is outside the range the rule was validated against: ...`. With `--verbose`, the rules whose crate no package depends on are counted.
- The withheld-rule sentence states its criterion: `... left out of what to fix first: the corpus found it wrong on most of the sites it reviewed.`
- The agent hand-off prompt names the rules holding the ceiling from `audit.score.ceilings`, so a test-only finding is no longer named ([1f6799a](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/1f6799a)).

## A scan survives its input

- A multibyte character just before `://` in a tracked file, a code frame or a build script's stderr no longer crashes the credential scanner ([d6060ed](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/d6060ed)).
- `--json` writes the whole document or nothing. A child process nobody waited on is killed with its process group (`SIGKILL` on Unix, `taskkill /F /T` on Windows). The interactive report's text wrap always advances, where a double-width character in a one-column panel looped forever ([d6060ed](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/d6060ed)).
- Source text is parsed as rustc reads it: a leading byte order mark is dropped and each CRLF becomes LF. On a CRLF checkout, the Git for Windows default, every multi-line string literal used to fail to parse, the report came back incomplete, and the contextual scope lost the function around a finding ([6bcdfc9](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/6bcdfc9)).
- Two overlapping scans of one workspace without a `Cargo.lock` take turns, instead of leaving an untracked `Cargo.lock` behind or failing with `failed to open: ./Cargo.lock`. On Unix the turn is a `flock` on the workspace directory. On Windows it is a `rust-doctor-lockfile-<hash>.lock` file in the temporary directory, one per workspace, left in place. A second scan waits until the first is done, or until `--max-duration` or a signal stops it, and then leaves the lockfile alone ([742a0b0](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/742a0b0)).
- On Unix, a SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP during the interactive report always ends the run with 130. On macOS the run could end with the scan's own code instead. A run a signal stopped launches no agent and copies no prompt ([3fc935f](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/3fc935f)).

## Smaller fixes

- The report and the Cargo stderr excerpt replace a path only where its last component ends. `~/.cargo-target` no longer reads `$CARGO_HOME-target`, and a sibling `project-member` of the workspace `project` no longer reads `.-member` ([1815242](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/1815242)).
- Without `--advisory-db`, the RustSec database read is the clone fetched most recently, by `.git/FETCH_HEAD`. A `cargo deny` clone wins only when it is strictly newer than the `cargo audit` one, and `--advisory-db` still wins over both ([50975a4](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/50975a4)).
- `timings.clippy_dependencies` ends at the last dependency artifact, not the first member's, and the two Clippy phases always add up to the run ([7272520](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7272520)).
- The Markdown report escapes a not-evaluated rule id that is not a catalogued one. A saved report holding a crafted id could otherwise publish its own markup in a pull request comment ([329fbca](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/329fbca)).

## Installation and toolchain

- `cargo binstall rust-doctor` installs a prebuilt binary instead of compiling. Each GitHub Release now carries `rust-doctor-<target>.tar.gz` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. The archives are packed reproducibly from the binaries npm ships, the release is immutable once published, and `[package.metadata.binstall]` disables QuickInstall (#41, [5a20644](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/5a20644)).
- The README advertises `cargo install rust-doctor --locked`. Without `--locked`, Cargo ignores the shipped `Cargo.lock` and can resolve a dependency graph that does not compile (#40, [1cbcd2d](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/1cbcd2d)).
- The validated toolchain moves from 1.97.1 to 1.99.1: it is the default of the Action's `toolchain` input and of `rust-doctor ci install --toolchain`. A workflow `ci install` wrote before picks it up with `rust-doctor ci install --update` ([7fc9445](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7fc9445)).

## Library

The crate's source no longer carries comments, so the library pages on docs.rs have no prose. The CLI `--help` output is unchanged ([7991b7a](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7991b7a)). Schema 24 adds the public type `rust_doctor::ScoreCeiling`, the public fields `AuditScore::ceilings` and `AuditCategory::production`, and `Audit::production_totals()`. Code that builds those structs with struct-literal syntax has to name the new fields ([8774eb6](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8774eb6)).

## Internal

The tree carries no comment or shebang, and a test fails on any that returns. Every `unsafe` block states its invariant in an `#[expect(clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks, reason = ...)]`, and the npm bin gets its shebang when it is packed ([7991b7a](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7991b7a)). CI pins toolchain 1.99.1 everywhere ([7fc9445](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7fc9445)) and runs the end-to-end and corpus jobs on ubuntu-26.04 ([4d1057a](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/4d1057a)). A daily workflow installs without `--locked` ([1cbcd2d](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/1cbcd2d)), and the release proves `cargo binstall` before and after it publishes ([5a20644](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/5a20644)). Flaky tests were fixed: self-scans kept off the structure clock, a stand-in cargo that raced its own probes, and a tmux shell typed into before its prompt ([ad28912](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/ad28912), [687b1b8](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/687b1b8), [bcc23a3](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/bcc23a3), [ff0b929](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/ff0b929), [98e608b](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/98e608b)). The remaining commits are the self-scan remediation PRD, its certifications and documentation corrections.

## Install

```bash
npx rust-doctor@latest
```

```bash
cargo install rust-doctor --locked
```

```bash
cargo binstall rust-doctor
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/compare/v0.9.0...v0.10.0
